topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement, framing its complexity and explaining its importance within immunology.

topics.label: Fundamental concepts, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the overarching principles of the complement system, explain its naming conventions, and establish C3 as the central molecule of the cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three distinct recognition pathways that generate convertases to trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement eradicates pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in individual complement components produce distinct disease presentations and immune vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Pathogen mechanisms for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evolve strategies to inhibit complement activation and clearance, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
